system:
You answer questions about company SEC filings (10-K and 10-Q) using ONLY the pages provided.
Each page starts with a header line naming the company, form, fiscal year, doc id and page number.
Read the numbers you need from the pages and do any arithmetic yourself.

Reply with one JSON object and nothing else:
{"answer": short answer as a string,
 "value": the answer as a number, a string, a list of company names, or null,
 "unit": one of "USD", "ratio", "shares", "count", "text", "company", "USD/share", "none",
 "abstain": true or false,
 "facts_used": [{"doc": doc id from the page header, "page": page number from the header,
                 "value": the number as a plain number in full units, "label": the line item}]}

Rules
- Numbers in full units: if a table says "in millions", 1,234 means 1234000000. No commas, no symbols.
- Ratios, margins, growth rates and percentages as fractions: 12.5% is 0.125, unit "ratio".
- Per-share amounts: unit "USD/share", value in dollars per share.
- Questions asking which company or for a ranking: value is a list of company names in the order
  asked (one name if one company is asked for), unit "company".
- Names, places and other words: value is a string, unit "text".
- If the pages do not contain what is needed to answer, set "abstain": true and "value": null.
  Do not guess and do not use outside knowledge.
- facts_used lists every number from the pages that you used, with its doc id and page.

The Company’s accounting policy related to advertising costs for annual reporting purposes is to expense production costs of print, radio, television and other advertisements as
of the first date the advertisements take place. All other marketing expenditures are expensed in the annual period in which the expenditure is incurred.
For quarterly reporting purposes, we allocate our estimated full year marketing expenditures that benefit multiple quarters to each of those quarters. We use the proportion of
each quarter’s actual unit case volume to the estimated full year unit case volume as the basis for the allocation. This methodology results in our marketing expenditures being
recognized at a standard rate per unit case. At the end of each quarter, we review our estimated full year unit case volume and our estimated full year marketing expenditures
that benefit multiple quarters in order to evaluate if a change in estimate is necessary. The impact of any change in the full year estimate is recognized in the quarter in which
the change in estimate occurs. Our full year marketing expenditures are not impacted by this interim accounting policy.

answer.answer: No, the latest 10-K (FY2025 10-K) reports the December 31, 2024 balance for prepaid expenses and other current assets as $2,998 million, which is different from the originally reported $3,129 million in the FY2024 10-K.
